short: The Russian Second Army was nearly destroyed by German forces in East Prussia during the war's opening weeks.
full:
On 26 August 1914, German forces under Paul von Hindenburg and Erich Ludendorff engaged the invading Russian Second Army near Tannenberg in East Prussia. Benefiting from intercepted, unencrypted Russian radio messages and exploiting the separation between two Russian armies, the Germans launched a devastating double envelopment. Over four days, the Russian army was encircled and effectively annihilated.

The victory saved East Prussia from Russian occupation and established Hindenburg and Ludendorff as national heroes in Germany. It forced the Russians to abandon their offensive into Germany and reorient their forces defensively, setting the tone for a long, brutal conflict on the Eastern Front that ultimately bled the Russian Empire to revolution.
